answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each agent identity holds a public log of completed tasks, each signed and timestamped like berths along a wharf. Any new identity must reproduce that history from genesis; duplicate copies of one operator's work collide on overlapping timestamps and diverge at a shared grove of prior checkpoints. Verification nodes compare logs against a trellis of cross-linked receipts, so a cloned identity must pay to regenerate or fork distinct genuine work per copy, making each sybil roughly as costly as operating a real agent.
